title: Routed latency twinboard: p50/p95/p99 + streaming vs blocking cohorts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a twin dashboard that surfaces per-model and per-route latency percentiles (p50 / p95 / p99) with an explicit streaming vs blocking (non-streaming) breakdown. The board must combine metrics, sampled traces, and log snippets so engineers can quickly move from percentile spikes to root-cause traces and associated logs. It should also support cohorting by request shape (input tokens, output tokens), client SDK, and KV-cache hit/miss to show economic and performance trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 for selected model(s) and route(s) over selectable time windows (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d)
Explicit toggle to split series by IO mode: streaming vs blocking; each series has its own percentiles
Cohort filters: request length bucket, output token bucket, client SDK label, KV cache status; applying a cohort updates metrics and trace sampling filter
Trace links included: clicking an anomalous percentile point should open sampled trace(s) + waterfall and attach relevant logs (if available)
Overlay synthetic-sla line and prior-release baseline for quick regression checks
Dashboard has permissive performance: initial query refresh <= 3s for 24h window and <= 7s for 7d window on prod telemetry cluster
Unit and integration tests for query correctness + feature flag gating for rollout
notes: Design: collaborate with Design for a twin-panel layout (left: percentile heatlines + cohort selector, right: trace/flow explorer for selected point). See design sketch: https://drive.redwood/designs/observability/twinboard-sketch

Metrics: use existing route/model tags in metrics namespace (redwood.latency.*). New tag expected: io_mode {streaming, blocking}. If missing, add instrumentation in route router to set io_mode based on request metadata.
Tracing: add a high-cardinality attribute 'request_shape' (small|medium|large) computed in the frontdoor sampler to aid quick cohort selection without full-text parsing
Sampling: increase sampling of error traces for p99 windows and add a temporary synthetic-sampler for rollout weeks to ensure coverage
KV cache overlay: use cache.hit and cache.miss counters; compute derived series for % hit by cohort and show side-by-side impact on p95
Costs: be mindful of increased trace volume; coordinate with infra to provision temporary retention if spike occurs during rollout
